Or in full: Impatience, Laziness, and Hubris are the three programmer virtues. Impatience is the virtue I want to extol unto you today, because of some experiences I've had lately.

In particular, tonight I spent some time with some extraordinarily boring people. Incommunicative, and when they did have something to say, it was tedious. Their witlessness was suffocating, and made me think (by contrast, mind you) of that peculiar, electric quality of properly thriving chan-boards.

We're often patient with the wrong things. Not just boring people, but boring ideas, too. We ask questions we already know the answers to. Repeat the same mistakes. Intellectual laziness isn't just dishonesty, but is also when you fail to apply the basic logical arithmetic that you already understand.

Safety is stultifying. Watching reruns is perhaps the epitome of being sucked into a comfortable undertow of routine. What's worse, a waterlogged brain is only dimly cognizant that it has become stultified.

And that, I find, makes the air sweeter when you finally resurface. It's also easy to forget that the time you lose down there is non-refundable. That's why it's important to stay a little bit angry.

This is your life, and it's ending one minute at a time.
Patience is for people who are comfortable with a lack of progress.
